title: Confronting the Challenges of Participatory Culture

doab.title: Confronting the Challenges of Participatory Culture
doab.series_name: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation Reports on Digital Media and Learning

abstract: Many teens today who use the Internet are actively involved in participatory cultures—joining online communities (Facebook, message boards, game clans), producing creative work in new forms (digital sampling, modding, fan videomaking, fan fiction), working in teams to complete tasks and develop new knowledge (as in Wikipedia), and shaping the flow of media (as in blogging or podcasting). A growing body of scholarship suggests potential benefits of these activities, including opportunities for peer-to-peer learning, development of skills useful in the modern workplace, and a more empowered conception of citizenship. Some argue that young people pick up these key skills and competencies on their own by interacting with popular culture; but the problems of unequal access, lack of media transparency, and the breakdown of traditional forms of socialization and professional training suggest a role for policy and pedagogical intervention. This report aims to shift the conversation about the "digital divide" from questions about access to technology to questions about access to opportunities for involvement in participatory culture and how to provide all young people with the chance to develop the cultural competencies and social skills needed. Fostering these skills, the authors argue, requires a systemic approach to media education; schools, afterschool programs, and parents all have distinctive roles to play. The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation Reports on Digital Media and Learning

narrative:
Short impact summary

Confronting the Challenges of Participatory Culture (2009), published by The MIT Press, has been cited 2,232 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it is discussed on Hypothes.is.

Full narrative

Confronting the Challenges of Participatory Culture by Henry Jenkins, Ravi Purushotma, Margaret Weigel and others was published by The MIT Press in 2009. It is part of the The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation Reports on Digital Media and Learning series. Conceptually, the work connects to Participatory culture, Public relations, Citizen journalism, Social media and Scholarship.

OpenAlex records 2,232 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2019 with 171 citing works. Notable citing venues include IGI Global eBooks, Advances in educational technologies and instructional design book series and Journal of Adolescent & Adult Literacy. Of 896 citation statements scite has classified, 6 support its claims, 756 mention it in passing, and none contradict it. The citing works include 1,313 journal articles, 585 book chapters and 28 preprints. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, Spain and Germany.

It is discussed on Hypothes.is (2 mentions). Open Library reports a combined count of 3 reading logs and catalog editions. A further 2 mentions appear in other attention signals. Its subject matter aligns with Quality Education among the Sustainable Development Goals.

The latest English Wikipedia check verified 7 article–work reference matches. These are references or bibliography entries, which may include other editions of the same work; they do not measure readership.
